title: Generic-point product description of the meromorphic sheaf
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let X^0 be the set of generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of X. Assume (a) every weakly associated point of X is the generic point of an irreducible component, where a point is weakly associated when the maximal ideal of its local ring is weakly associated to that local ring, meaning it is minimal among the prime ideals containing the annihilator of some element, and (b) every quasi-compact open of X has finitely many irreducible components. Let K_X be the sheaf obtained by localizing O_X at its non-zero-divisors, and let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For each generic point eta write j_eta: Spec(O_{X,eta}) \to X for the canonical morphism. Then K_X = product_{eta in X^0} j_{eta,*} O_{X,eta} and K_X(F) = K_X tensor_{O_X} F = product_{eta in X^0} j_{eta,*} F_eta.

proof.text: Work on an affine open U = Spec(A). The irreducible components of U correspond to the finitely many minimal primes q_1, ..., q_t of A, and their generic points are exactly the points represented by these primes. The hypothesis on quasi-compact opens gives the required finiteness. By [lem-sc-affine-weakass-nonzerodivisors], the non-zero-divisors of A are the complement of the union of the weakly associated primes; a prime p of A is weakly associated to A if and only if the point p of U is a weakly associated point of X, i.e. pA_p is weakly associated to A_p = O_{X,p} (elementary, Algebra Lemma 10.66.2, tag 0566: localization is exact, so the annihilator of a/s in A_p is Ann_A(a)A_p, and the primes of A_p are the primes of A contained in p, so p is minimal over Ann_A(a) exactly when pA_p is minimal over Ann_A(a)A_p). Hypothesis (a) therefore puts every weakly associated prime of A among the generic points of irreducible components of X lying in U, which are exactly the generic points of the irreducible components of U, i.e. among the q_i. The affine total-quotient calculation [lem-sc-affine-totalquotient-minimal-product] then gives Q(A) = product_i A_{q_i}.

source.place: Tag 0EMF, proof: affine open Spec(A), finite minimal primes, and Algebra Lemmas 10.66.7 (tag 05C3), 10.66.2 (tag 0566) and 10.25.4 (tag 02LX)

proof.text: For U = Spec(A), the value of the localization presheaf defining K_X is Q(A). For a generic point eta_i represented by q_i, the inverse image of U under j_{eta_i}: Spec(O_{X,eta_i}) \to X is Spec(A_{q_i}), so the value of j_{eta_i,*} O_{X,eta_i} on U is A_{q_i}; if eta_i is not in U the value is zero. Thus the affine isomorphism in Step 1 is exactly K_X(U) = product_{eta in X^0 intersect U} j_{eta,*} O_{X,eta}(U). These identifications agree on inclusions of affine opens, so the affine-basis equalities glue to K_X = product_{eta in X^0} j_{eta,*} O_{X,eta}.

source.place: Tag 0EMF, proof: identify the affine presheaf with j_* O_Y and conclude the sheaf isomorphism

proof.text: Let F be quasi-coherent and write M = F(U) on an affine U = Spec(A). Tensoring the finite product decomposition of Step 1 with M gives K_X(U) tensor_A M = (product_i A_{q_i}) tensor_A M = product_i (A_{q_i} tensor_A M) = product_i M_{q_i}; the middle equality is finite distributivity of tensor products over finite products. The factor M_{q_i} is the stalk F_{eta_i}, and the same restriction compatibility as in Step 2 identifies the resulting affine maps with the canonical map K_X tensor_{O_X} F \to product_{eta in X^0} j_{eta,*} F_eta. Hence K_X(F) = product_{eta in X^0} j_{eta,*} F_eta.
